newsitem.title: FINLAND: SAK HAS 26-POINT PLAN TO CUT FINNISH UNEMPLOYMENT.
newsitem.headline: SAK HAS 26-POINT PLAN TO CUT FINNISH UNEMPLOYMENT.

text.p: The Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) on Monday unveiled a package of proposals to halve unemployment by 1999, saying the measures would hardly increase public sector costs at all.
SAK -- with 1.1 million mainly blue-collar members Finland's biggest central trade union group -- presented to the government a 26-point programme to halve the jobless rate.
"These measures would hardly have any cost effects because most of the proposals are based on the reallocation of resources," SAK said in a statement.
Economic growth was strong and prospects for the coming years were positive, it said.
"The employment target must not be given up," SAK said, referring to the left-right-green government's stated objective to halve the unemployment rate to 8-9 percent by the end of its term in 1999.
SAK said the benefits of strong growth should be used to boost employment, and corporate profits should not be distributed as "excessive dividends".
-- cut personal income tax and shift the emphasis of taxation to real estate, capital gains, wealth and assets and environmental taxes,
-- lower the value added tax in labour-intensive service sectors,
-- promote job sharing, and in the medium term cut the working week to 30 hours from 37.5-40 hours currently,
-- to strenghten the production base and raise the degree of refinement of the mechanical forest industry,
-- to maintain and upgrade transport infrastructure like railways, highways, harbours and airports, and information technology networks.
